clinicalPearls: Represents the intermediate-severity phenotype within the cryopyrin-associated periodic syndrome spectrum, sitting between familial cold autoinflammatory syndrome and neonatal-onset multisystem inflammatory disease.
Caused by autosomal dominant gain-of-function variants in NLRP3 encoding cryopyrin; de novo variants and somatic mosaicism both occur.
The rash is a neutrophilic urticarial dermatosis: migrating wheals that burn or sting rather than itch, are not relieved by antihistamines and are not consistently cold-provoked.
Progressive sensorineural hearing loss is a hallmark and a key reason for early recognition, as it can be halted by timely treatment.
Recurrent low-grade fever, fatigue, conjunctivitis, headache and large-joint arthralgia accompany the cutaneous features.
Reactive AA amyloidosis, presenting with proteinuria and progressive renal impairment, is the most serious long-term complication.
Interleukin-1 blockade produces a rapid and often dramatic response and can prevent progression of both hearing loss and amyloidosis when started early.
A raised neutrophil count and persistently elevated acute-phase reactants with serum amyloid A are typical even between overt flares.
reference.pathophysiology: Gain-of-function variants in NLRP3 render the cryopyrin inflammasome hypersensitive so that it assembles with minimal or no exogenous trigger. Constitutive activation of caspase-1 drives excessive maturation and secretion of interleukin-1 beta and interleukin-18, producing systemic and neutrophil-rich tissue inflammation. In the cochlea, chronic interleukin-1-mediated inflammation damages the organ of hearing, accounting for progressive sensorineural deafness, while sustained hepatic serum amyloid A production leads to AA amyloid deposition, particularly in the kidney. Somatic mosaicism of NLRP3 can produce the phenotype despite a negative conventional germline genetic test.
additionalDifferentials: Systemic juvenile idiopathic arthritis and adult-onset Still's disease
Other hereditary recurrent fevers such as familial Mediterranean fever
additionalInvestigations: NLRP3 gene analysis including testing for somatic mosaicism when germline sequencing is negative
Pure-tone audiometry with periodic monitoring for sensorineural hearing loss
Skin biopsy demonstrating a perivascular and interstitial neutrophilic infiltrate
Acute-phase reactants including C-reactive protein and serum amyloid A
Urinalysis for proteinuria and tissue biopsy with Congo red staining if amyloidosis is suspected
Ophthalmological review for conjunctivitis and optic disc changes
redFlags: New or worsening sensorineural hearing loss indicating active cochlear inflammation
Persistently elevated inflammatory markers despite apparent clinical quiescence
Papilloedema or visual symptoms suggesting evolution towards the severe end of the spectrum
reference.prognosis: Early and sustained interleukin-1 blockade controls inflammation, preserves hearing and markedly reduces the risk of amyloidosis, allowing a good quality of life. Delayed treatment risks irreversible deafness and renal failure from amyloidosis.
pitfalls: Mistaking the neutrophilic urticarial rash for allergic urticaria and persisting with ineffective antihistamines
Attributing insidious hearing loss to unrelated causes and missing the therapeutic window
Concluding the diagnosis is excluded by a negative germline NLRP3 test when somatic mosaicism is possible
Underestimating amyloidosis risk because overt flares appear infrequent
references: Firestein & Kelley's Textbook of Rheumatology (current edition)
SHARE recommendations for the management of autoinflammatory diseases
Textbook of Pediatric Rheumatology, Cassidy (current edition)
management: Interleukin-1 blockade is the mainstay, using anakinra, canakinumab or rilonacept to suppress the constitutively active inflammasome, control symptoms and preserve hearing
Start and sustain treatment early, before irreversible cochlear damage or amyloid deposition occurs
Monitor hearing with serial pure-tone audiometry and provide hearing aids or cochlear implants for established sensorineural loss
Surveil for reactive AA amyloidosis with urinalysis for proteinuria, renal function and serum amyloid A
Titrate the interleukin-1 inhibitor to keep acute-phase reactants suppressed, escalating dose if inflammation persists
Offer genetic counselling for this autosomal dominant NLRP3 disorder, testing for somatic mosaicism if germline sequencing is negative
Coordinate multidisciplinary care across rheumatology, audiology and nephrology
